cards.title: Sound Hunt Basket
cards.how_to_play: Take a small basket on a walk around the garden or a nearby street, stopping every few steps to listen. Each time you hear something — a car, a bird, a gate creaking — pop a matching picture card or small object into the basket. Back inside, tip out the basket and see who can remember what made each sound.
cards.two_year_olds: Keep walks short and stay close: point to a sound and name it together ('Listen, a bird!'). Two-year-olds are not expected to name sounds on their own yet.

cards.title: Freeze and Point
cards.how_to_play: Play outdoors or on a walk. Every time the adult rings a small bell, children freeze on the spot and silently point towards where the last sound they heard came from, then whisper what it was.
cards.two_year_olds: Keep walks short and stay close: point to a sound and name it together ('Listen, a bird!'). Two-year-olds are not expected to name sounds on their own yet.

cards.title: Sound Box Guess
cards.how_to_play: Fill several opaque boxes with everyday objects that make a sound when shaken — keys, dried pasta, a squeaky toy — hidden behind a screen. Children take turns listening to a shake and guessing what's inside before it's revealed.
cards.two_year_olds: Keep walks short and stay close: point to a sound and name it together ('Listen, a bird!'). Two-year-olds are not expected to name sounds on their own yet.

cards.title: Instrument Corner Guess
cards.how_to_play: Sit children in a circle with a screen or blanket hiding a small set of instruments — drum, bells, shaker, tambourine. Play one out of sight and children guess which instrument it was, then reveal it and pass it round the circle.
cards.two_year_olds: Offer two instruments at a time. Let them play freely first, then copy you: loud, then quiet.

cards.title: Loud and Quiet March
cards.how_to_play: Give every child a homemade shaker, such as a bottle with rice inside. March around the room together, playing loud when the adult holds up a big sun picture and quiet when a small cloud picture is held up.
cards.two_year_olds: Offer two instruments at a time. Let them play freely first, then copy you: loud, then quiet.

cards.title: Copy My Pattern
cards.how_to_play: The adult taps a simple rhythm on a drum, such as tap-tap-pause-tap, and children copy it back on their own instrument. Build up to slightly longer, trickier patterns as the group succeeds.
cards.two_year_olds: Offer two instruments at a time. Let them play freely first, then copy you: loud, then quiet.

cards.title: Body Sound Orchestra
cards.how_to_play: Stand in a circle and go round naming a body sound in turn — clap, stamp, click, pat knees. Once everyone has chosen a sound, the adult 'conducts' by pointing to different children to build up a whole-group rhythm.
cards.two_year_olds: Copy one simple action at a time (clap, then pat your knees). Keep any pattern to one or two beats.

cards.title: Echo Me
cards.how_to_play: The adult claps or stamps a short pattern, such as clap-clap-stamp, and children echo it back exactly. Patterns get a little longer and trickier as the game continues.
cards.two_year_olds: Copy one simple action at a time (clap, then pat your knees). Keep any pattern to one or two beats.

cards.title: Freeze Dance Body Beats
cards.how_to_play: Play music and let children clap, stamp and pat along freely. When the music stops, everyone freezes and the adult calls out one body sound, such as 'clicks!', for children to make three of before the music starts again.
cards.two_year_olds: Copy one simple action at a time (clap, then pat your knees). Keep any pattern to one or two beats.

cards.title: Rhyme Basket Match
cards.how_to_play: Fill a basket with pairs of small objects or picture cards that rhyme, such as cat and hat, star and car. Children pull two out at a time, say them aloud, and decide whether they rhyme, sorting them into a 'yes' pile and a 'no' pile.
cards.two_year_olds: Sing the same few rhymes every day and pause before a familiar word for them to fill in. Joining in matters more than making up rhymes.

cards.title: Beat the Bongo
cards.how_to_play: Sing a familiar nursery rhyme together while children pat the steady beat on their knees or a small drum. Every few lines, pause and have the group clap the beat alone before the singing continues.
cards.two_year_olds: Sing the same few rhymes every day and pause before a familiar word for them to fill in. Joining in matters more than making up rhymes.

cards.title: Silly Rhyme Swap
cards.how_to_play: Sing a well-known rhyme but swap the last rhyming word for a made-up nonsense word that still rhymes, for example 'Jack and Jill went up the... zill'. Children put their hands up when they spot the swap and suggest their own silly word.
cards.two_year_olds: Sing the same few rhymes every day and pause before a familiar word for them to fill in. Joining in matters more than making up rhymes.

cards.title: Clap Your Name
cards.how_to_play: Sit in a circle. Say each child's name slowly and clap once for each beat: Ra-hul (two claps), Sam (one), Ol-i-ver (three). Everyone joins in, then ask, 'How many claps in your name?' A wrong count is just another go.
cards.two_year_olds: Clap along to names and songs together and enjoy the beat. Counting beats is for three- and four-year-olds.

cards.title: Beat Basket
cards.how_to_play: Fill a basket with familiar things that have one, two or three beats: cup, teddy, banana, umbrella. Pull one out, say its name together and tap the beats on your knees, then put it on a mat marked with one, two or three dots.
cards.two_year_olds: Clap along to names and songs together and enjoy the beat. Counting beats is for three- and four-year-olds.

cards.title: Stepping Stone Beats
cards.how_to_play: Lay out hoops or mats as stepping stones. Say a word and jump one stone for each beat: di-no-saur (three jumps), ap-ple (two), frog (one). Then let a child choose a word for everyone to jump.
cards.two_year_olds: Clap along to names and songs together and enjoy the beat. Counting beats is for three- and four-year-olds.

cards.title: Silly Soup
cards.how_to_play: The adult pretends to stir a big pretend cooking pot and invites children to add a silly ingredient that starts with today's chosen sound, for example 'I'm putting in a banana, a ball and a bear!'. The sillier the better.
cards.two_year_olds: Play with silly sounds in songs ('ba-ba-banana!'). Spotting words that start the same comes later, at three and four.

cards.title: Matching Sound Table
cards.how_to_play: Lay out a mix of small toys and objects on a table, where several share the same starting sound. Children sort them into groups by their starting sound, saying each object's name aloud as they go.
cards.two_year_olds: Play with silly sounds in songs ('ba-ba-banana!'). Spotting words that start the same comes later, at three and four.

cards.title: Name Sound Parade
cards.how_to_play: Line children up and say each child's name with a matching silly adjective that starts with the same sound, for example 'Bouncy Beth' or 'Terrific Tom'. Children then march around the room calling out their own.
cards.two_year_olds: Play with silly sounds in songs ('ba-ba-banana!'). Spotting words that start the same comes later, at three and four.

cards.title: Volume Dial
cards.how_to_play: Hold up a hand and 'turn' an imaginary dial from low to high while children match their voice volume to where your hand is pointing, from a whisper right up to a controlled loud voice.
cards.two_year_olds: Lots of animal and vehicle noises: they copy you, and you copy them. This is one of the best games at this age.

cards.title: Giant and Mouse Voices
cards.how_to_play: Take turns being a giant, using a low, slow, booming voice, and a mouse, using a high, quick, squeaky voice, saying the same simple phrase each time. Switch back and forth on a signal from the adult.
cards.two_year_olds: Lots of animal and vehicle noises: they copy you, and you copy them. This is one of the best games at this age.

cards.title: Long Sound Balloon
cards.how_to_play: Pretend to blow up a balloon while making a long, stretched-out sound such as 'aaaaaah', getting a little longer with each pretend breath. Then let the 'balloon' go with one short, sudden sound to pop it.
cards.two_year_olds: Lots of animal and vehicle noises: they copy you, and you copy them. This is one of the best games at this age.

cards.title: Robot Talk Snack Time
cards.how_to_play: At snack or tidy-up time, give simple instructions in a robot voice, breaking the key word into sounds, for example 'pass the c-u-p'. Children blend the sounds together to work out what's needed and respond.
cards.two_year_olds: Not yet. Blending sounds by ear is for three- and four-year-olds and Reception. With two-year-olds, play the voice and rhyme games instead.

cards.title: Puppet Says the Sounds
cards.how_to_play: A puppet 'talks funny' and says familiar objects in separated sounds, such as d-o-g or s-u-n. Children shout out the blended word as fast as they can to 'help' the puppet be understood.
cards.two_year_olds: Not yet. Blending sounds by ear is for three- and four-year-olds and Reception. With two-year-olds, play the voice and rhyme games instead.

cards.title: Break It Down Bag
cards.how_to_play: Pull an object from a feely bag and say its name normally, then together with the children clap and say each sound separately, such as c-a-t, counting how many sounds and claps the word has.
cards.two_year_olds: Not yet. Blending sounds by ear is for three- and four-year-olds and Reception. With two-year-olds, play the voice and rhyme games instead.
